pages.text: Rice paddies stepped down like stairs. Water trickled from upper fields to lower ones. Bubbles floated along in lines.
The little top patch was Dingding's. Its floor was cracked and dry. "I want water in my field too."
Grandma brought a shovel. "The water channel is beneath here." "Really?"
She dug the earthen path between fields—the paddy bank. Only soil came out. "A little deeper."
Grandma straightened. "The channel used to be here."
Soil piled at the hole. Dingding's field stayed dry. Dingding crouched on the bank.
More bubbles passed. Dingding followed them with both eyes. All went one way.
Water trickled beyond the bank. "Grandma! The water moved here!"
She pushed a little soil aside. Water poured in, bubbles circling Dingding's field. "The channel is busier than I am."
